text:
alex: heads up — I'm proposing a "budgeted head/tail" sampling approach for the OTEL ingestion pipeline. short doc: https://rwd-internal/sampling/budgeted-headtail (TL;DR below). looking for quick feedback before i spin up a staging prototype.

mika: reading — quick q: how is "budgeted" different from per-route dynamic sampling we've chatted about?

alex: good call. difference: instead of continuously shifting prob across routes, we give each route/customer-tier a short-lived token budget that pays for tail retention. head sampling stays deterministic for errors/latency spikes. budgets replenish on a sliding window. idea is to bound cost while preserving tail visibility for high-impact routes.

priya: sounds promising. curious about exporter backpressure — if budgets exhaust and we drop spans, do exporters get overloaded when they re-enable? any smoothing?

alex: plan is to add a small reservoir + exponential backoff for burst replays. also a soft-degraded mode where we downgrade full traces to span-metadata-only to reduce size.

sam: can you paste the rough policy schema? i want to see if our current sampling-controller can apply it without a restart.

alex: sure — here's a draft policy shape we tested locally:`
```yaml
policy_version: 1
routes:
  - match: "/api/v1/generate"
    tier: gold
    head_sampling: 
      keep_errors: true
      keep_early_spans: true
    budget:
      tokens_per_minute: 200
      token_cost:
        tail_trace: 10
        partial_trace: 3
    reservoir: 5
  - match: "/api/v1/embeddings"
    tier: silver
    head_sampling:
      keep_errors: true
    budget:
      tokens_per_minute: 50
      token_cost:
        tail_trace: 12
        partial_trace: 4
    reservoir: 2
global:
  fallback_sample_rate: 0.002
  downgrade_on_budget_exhaust: true
```

priya: nice. if the controller supports hot-reload via control-plane config, we can flip policies per-tenant. would prefer RBAC so only platform can change budget caps.

emily: UX concern for Console: we need metrics and a simple view for "budget health" per-route and per-customer. e.g., sampled_rate, budget_remaining, tail_traces_retained, partial_traces_dropped. want to be able to set alerts when budget dips under X.

sam: agree. also add a histogram of trace sizes pre/post-downgrade so we can verify downgrade wins.

mika: what's the SLO impact? if we drop tail traces for lower tiers, are we still able to triage incidents?

alex: head sampling keeps all errors/latency outliers for all routes. tails are mainly for behavioural analysis and regression hunting — gold/silver keep most tails via budget. cheap-tier gets rare tail retention. we want to preserve signal for incident triage: errors -> always kept. non-error tails are best-effort.

ci-bot: test run: sampling-policy-linter failed on policy schema v1. Error: "token_cost" expected numeric but got string at routes[0].budget.token_cost.tail_trace

alex: ack — my bad, example had inconsistent types. i'll fix and push a corrected doc.

priya: one more ops question: retention and exporters. If we downgrade to metadata-only spans, do our BigQuery or ClickHouse exporters need schema changes?

alex: exporters will need to accept a span-level 'downgrade_level' flag and route metadata-only items to 'trace_meta' tables. minimal schema change: add nullable fields for full_payload and metadata_only boolean. plan to gate this behind a feature flag.

emily: for Console rollout, propose two-stage: (1) expose sampling policy and live budget metrics in beta for platform team; (2) enable per-tenant toggles for customers with > X throughput. that way product can approve before wide release.

sam: can we simulate cost effects? want an offline runner to replay week of traces with candidate policies and output expected token burn + cost delta.

alex: yes — i built a replay CLI that outputs token usage and retained-trace-set for a policy. will push to the repo and attach a run for the last 7 days traffic of staging.

mika: deployment plan? I'm worried about rollout causing a noisy flurry when budgets flip.

alex: rollout: start in staging, then opt-in tenants (gold), then canary 5% of traffic in prod for 48h, monitor budget burn and error triage time. failover: when budget errors increase or we see regression, instantly toggle fallback_sample_rate to 1/20th. ops can also switch to 'metadata-only' globally.

priya: ok — actions: alex to correct schema + push replay run; sam to add Console metrics list; emily to draft Console beta UX; mika to own canary monitor playbook.

alex: thanks everyone. will push updated doc + sample policy in 2 hrs. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: scheduled maintenance note — sampling-controller v0.3 will be deployable via canary flags tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

emily: noted. tagging @platform-oncall so they're aware. :eyes:
